COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
16.05.2025 CRLR No.127 of 2025
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Mr. Narendra Bali, learned counsel for the 
revisionist.
2. Present criminal revision is preferred against 
the judgment and order dated 03.02.2025 passed by 
learned Fourth Additional Sessions Judge, 
Haridwar in Criminal Appeal No.34 of 2024, 
“Krishnaveer Vs. State of Uttarakhand & Another”
as well as impugned judgment and order dated 
20.01.2024 passed by the learned Judicial 
Magistrate-I, Haridwar in Complaint Case (Old) 
No.3367 of 2015, Complaint Case (New) No.1339 
of 2022 “Sudesh Kumar Saini Vs. Krishnaveer”
punishable under Section 138 of Negotiable 
Instrument Act whereby the revisionist was 
convicted and sentenced to undergo three months 
simple imprisonment along with fine of 
₹18,30,000/- and in default of payment of fine to 
undergo further one month simple imprisonment 
additionally.
3. Learned counsel for the revisionist/convict 
would submit that judgment and orders of the 
Courts below suffer from perversity; that, the 
impugned judgment and orders of the Courts below 
are incorrect, improper and illegal and thus, 
deserve to be set-aside.
4. Issue notice to the respondent through 
ordinary process and registered post, 
acknowledgement due as well as by email and 
WhatsApp, if available.
5. Steps to be taken within two weeks. 
6. Heard on the bail and suspension of 
sentence. 
7. Learned counsel for the revisionist/convict 
would submit that the revisionist/convict is ready to 
deposit the entire amount of fine; that, the 
revisionist/convict is a law abiding person, he did 
not commit any offence and has been implicated in  this case with mala fide intention for taking undue 
advantage and he cannot defend himself by 
remaining in jail; that, the revisionist /convict may 
be exempted from surrendering and released on 
bail as the revision may take considerable time for 
its conclusion due to heavy pendency of cases.
8. Per contra, Counsel for the State opposed the 
bail application, however, submitted that if the 
revisionist /convict is ready to deposit the entire 
fine amount then bail application of the 
revisionist/convict may be considered.
9. Having considered the entirety of the facts 
and without expressing any final opinion on the 
merits of the case, the revisionist/convict is
exempted from surrendering and admitted to bail.
10. Let the revisionist/convict be released on 
bail, during the pendency of present criminal 
revision, on furnishing bail bond with two sureties 
in the amount of ₹50,000/- and personal bond of 
the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned 
Trial Court, subject to payment of the entire 
amount of fine by the revisionist/convict within one 
month from today.
The amount of fine so deposited in the Court 
be deposited in a fresh account of the case as 
opened in the MACT cases. 
11. Application for bail and suspension of 
sentence stands disposed of accordingly.
12. List this case on 08.08.2025 for hearing on 
admission.
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) 
 16.05.2025
SS

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
CRLR No.127 of 2025
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Narendra Bali, Advocate for the revisionist.
2. Mr. Parikshit Saini, Advocate for the respondent.
3. Today, the matter is listed on IA No.2 of 2025 i.e. 
the Bail Cancellation Application moved by the 
respondent.
4. It is contended by learned counsel for the 
respondent, Mr. Parikshit Saini that the bail was granted
to the revisionist by this Court vide order dated 
16.05.2025 which was a conditional order and before 
being released on bail, the revisionist was required to
deposit the amount of fine, as imposed by the learned 
Trial Court. But, without depositing the entire amount of 
fine, excluding the amount of 20% deposited by the 
revisionist during the pendency of the appeal, the 
revisionist was released on bail by the learned Magistrate. 
It appears that the learned Magistrate has misinterpreted 
the order passed by this Court, and without depositing the 
amount of fine as stated above, the revisionist was
released on bail.
5. Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that he 
would deposit the entire amount of fine as imposed by the 
learned Trial Court, excluding the 20% as deposited in the 
appellate court, within 15 days i.e. on or before 
31.07.2025. 
6. If the fine is not deposited within the time given by 
this Court to the revisionist today, the bail granted to him  2
earlier, shall stand rejected and he would be taken into 
custody for serving out the sentence.
7. List this case On 31.07.2025.
 
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 15.07.2025
Ravi

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
CRLR No.127 of 2025
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Narendra Bali, learned counsel for the revisionist.
2. Ms. Sukhwani Singh, learned counsel holding brief of 
Mr. Parikshit Saini, learned counsel for the respondent.
3. The revisionist was released on bail without 
complying the condition imposed by a Co-ordinate Bench of 
this Court wherein he has to deposit the fine imposed upon 
him i.e. 18,30,000/-. 
4. Surprisingly, the revisionist failed to deposit the 
amount of fine as stated above and still he has been 
released on bail by the learned trial court.
5. This Court vide order dated 15.07.2025 has been
pleased to pass the following order:-
“6. If the fine is not deposited within the time given by this 
Court to the revisionist today, the bail granted to him earlier, 
shall stand rejected and he would be taken into custody for 
serving out the sentence.”
6. In view of the order dated 15.07.2025, the bail 
granted to the revisionist already stands cancelled. 
Accordingly, no further order for cancellation of bail is 
required. Thus, the bail cancellation application (IA 
No.2/2025) stands disposed of.
7. Learned trial court is, therefore, directed to issue 
NBW against the revisionist to serve out the sentence.
8. List on 16.09.2025.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
31.07.2025 AK

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
CRLR No. 127 of 2025
Hon’ble Ashish Naithani, J.
Mr. Narendra Bali, learned counsel for the Revisionist. 
2. Ms. Sukhwani Singh, learned counsel holding brief of Mr. 
Parikshit Saini, learned counsel for the Respondent. 
3. Today, the matter is listed on the Urgency Application moved 
on behalf of the Revisionist.
4. Learned counsel for the Revisionist submits that, as per the 
order of this Court, an amount of ₹18,30,000/- was required to be 
deposited; however, the same could not be deposited within the 
stipulated time. It is further submitted that when the Revisionist
subsequently attempted to deposit the said amount, the learned Court 
below refused to accept the same.
5. Learned counsel for the Respondent, however, objects to the 
aforesaid submission and submits at the outset that the Revisionist has 
defaulted on several occasions and is in the habit of non-compliance. 
It is further contended that despite ample opportunities having been 
granted, the Revisionist has failed to comply with the orders of the 
Court.
6. In rejoinder, learned counsel for the Revisionist prays that three 
days’ time be granted for deposit of the said amount.
7. Learned counsel for the Respondent, in response, submits that 
if any indulgence is granted, strict conditions be imposed and a 
specific time limit be fixed.
8. In view of the above submissions, three working days’ time is 
accorded to the Revisionist to comply with the order of this Court.
9. List this case on 08.01.2026.
 (Ashish Naithani, J.) 
 03.01.2026
Shiksha
